title: ICSE CLASS 8 — Social Science | Parliament Government
description: Subject-wise test on Parliament Government (Social Science) for ICSE CLASS 8. 25Q.
subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the minimum age requirement for a person to be eligible to become a member of the Lok Sabha?

options.text: 18 years
options.explanation: 18 years is the voting age, not the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership.

options.text: 21 years
options.explanation: 21 years is the minimum age for membership in some local bodies but not for the Lok Sabha.

options.text: 25 years
options.explanation: Correct. The Constitution specifies 25 years as the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership.

options.text: 30 years
options.explanation: 30 years is the minimum age for membership in the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 84(b) of the Indian Constitution states that a person must be not less than 25 years of age to be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
questions.hint: The minimum age is higher than the voting age in India.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: The President of India
options.explanation: The President is the head of state but not the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: The Vice-President of India
options.explanation: Correct. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: The Prime Minister of India
options.explanation: The Prime Minister leads the executive but does not chair the Rajya Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 64 of the Indian Constitution states that the Vice-President shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
questions.hint: The position is held by a constitutional office holder who is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the normal term of office for a member of the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: 3 years
options.explanation: 3 years is the term for some local bodies but not the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: 4 years
options.explanation: 4 years is not the term for Rajya Sabha members.

options.text: 5 years
options.explanation: 5 years is the term for Lok Sabha members, not Rajya Sabha.

options.text: 6 years
options.explanation: Correct. Members of the Rajya Sabha serve a term of 6 years.

questions.explanation: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of six years, with one-third of its members retiring every two years, ensuring it is a permanent house.
questions.hint: The term is longer than that of the Lok Sabha.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: In which of the following Houses can a Money Bill be introduced?

options.text: Only in Lok Sabha
options.explanation: Correct. Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: Only in Rajya Sabha
options.explanation: Money Bills cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: In either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
options.explanation: Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: In a joint sitting of both Houses
options.explanation: Money Bills are not introduced in joint sittings.

questions.explanation: Article 109 of the Indian Constitution specifies that a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
questions.hint: Money Bills are financial in nature and originate in the directly elected house.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: The primary function of the Indian Parliament is to:

options.text: Implement laws passed by the Judiciary
options.explanation: The Parliament does not implement laws; it makes them.

options.text: Administer the country through its civil services
options.explanation: The civil services are administered by the executive branch, not the Parliament.

options.text: Make laws for the country and control the executive
options.explanation: Correct. The Parliament's primary functions are lawmaking and executive oversight.

options.text: Interpret the Constitution and settle disputes
options.explanation: The Judiciary interprets the Constitution and settles disputes, not the Parliament.

questions.explanation: The Parliament is the supreme legislative body responsible for enacting laws. It also exercises control over the Executive through various mechanisms like questions, discussions, and motions, ensuring accountability.
questions.hint: The Parliament's role includes both lawmaking and oversight of the executive.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'Question Hour' in the Indian Parliament?

options.text: It is the time when members vote on new laws.
options.explanation: Voting on laws occurs during other parliamentary proceedings.

options.text: It allows members to ask questions to ministers and hold the government accountable.
options.explanation: Correct. The Question Hour is for ministers to answer questions from MPs.

options.text: It is reserved for discussing private member bills.
options.explanation: Private member bills are discussed at other times.

options.text: It is when the President addresses a joint session of Parliament.
options.explanation: The President's address is a separate event.

questions.explanation: The Question Hour is the first hour of every parliamentary sitting where Members of Parliament ask questions to ministers about various aspects of administration and government policy, thereby holding the government accountable.
questions.hint: This hour is crucial for parliamentary accountability and transparency.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: If a No-Confidence Motion is passed against the Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha, what is the immediate consequence?

options.text: The Prime Minister has to resign, but the Council of Ministers remains.
options.explanation: The entire Council of Ministers must resign, not just the Prime Minister.

options.text: Only the minister against whom the motion was moved has to resign.
options.explanation: The motion is against the entire Council of Ministers, not an individual.

options.text: The entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, has to resign.
options.explanation: Correct. The government must resign as a whole.

options.text: The President dissolves the Lok Sabha immediately.
options.explanation: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha, but it is not an immediate consequence of a no-confidence motion.

questions.explanation: According to the principle of collective responsibility, if a no-confidence motion is passed against the Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha, it implies that the government has lost the confidence of the House, and the entire Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, must resign.
questions.hint: The principle of collective responsibility means the entire government is accountable to the Lok Sabha.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Members of the Rajya Sabha are primarily elected by:

options.text: Direct election by the people of India
options.explanation: Members are not directly elected by the people but by state legislatures.

options.text: Members of the State Legislative Assemblies
options.explanation: Correct. Rajya Sabha members are elected by state legislators.

options.text: The President of India on the advice of the Prime Minister
options.explanation: The President does not directly elect Rajya Sabha members.

options.text: The Chief Ministers of the respective states
options.explanation: Chief Ministers do not elect Rajya Sabha members; state legislators do.

questions.explanation: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union Territories through a system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
questions.hint: The Rajya Sabha represents the states, so its members are elected by state legislatures.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The Lok Sabha is more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in matters concerning the Union Budget.
**Reason (R):** A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha has limited powers regarding it.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha indeed has more power regarding the Union Budget (which is a Money Bill). Money Bills can only originate in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can only delay them for a maximum of 14 days or suggest amendments which the Lok Sabha is not bound to accept. Thus, the reason correctly explains why the Lok Sabha is more powerful in these financial matters.
questions.hint: The Lok Sabha's financial powers are greater due to the exclusive right to introduce Money Bills.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: A new bill, not a Money Bill, is introduced in the Lok Sabha and passed by it. It is then sent to the Rajya Sabha for consideration. What happens next?

options.text: The bill automatically becomes a law without the Rajya Sabha's approval.
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha must consider the bill; it does not automatically become law.

options.text: The Rajya Sabha can reject the bill, but the Lok Sabha can still pass it with a simple majority.
options.explanation: Correct. The Lok Sabha can override the Rajya Sabha's rejection by passing the bill again.

options.text: The bill is sent to the President for approval without the Rajya Sabha's consideration.
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha must consider the bill before it can be sent to the President.

options.text: The bill lapses if the Rajya Sabha does not pass it within 14 days.
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha has 6 months to consider a non-Money Bill, not 14 days.

questions.explanation: For a non-Money Bill, the Rajya Sabha can suggest amendments, reject the bill, or take no action. If the Rajya Sabha rejects or does not pass the bill within 6 months, the Lok Sabha can pass it again to make it a law, overriding the Rajya Sabha's rejection.
questions.hint: The Rajya Sabha has limited powers over non-Money Bills compared to Money Bills.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the maximum permissible strength of the Lok Sabha, including elected and nominated members, as per the original constitutional provision?

options.explanation: 250 is the minimum strength of the Rajya Sabha, not the Lok Sabha.
545 was the strength before the 104th Amendment Act, but the original provision allowed for 552.
This is the correct maximum strength as per the original constitutional provision.
530 is the maximum number of elected members from states, not the total strength.

questions.explanation: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is constitutionally fixed at 552 members, comprising up to 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the states, up to 20 members to represent the Union Territories, and 2 members nominated by the President from the Anglo-Indian community (this nomination provision was discontinued after the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019).
questions.hint: The correct answer includes the total number of members as per the original constitutional provision.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Who presides over the joint session of both Houses of the Indian Parliament?

options.text: The President of India
options.explanation: The President summons the joint session but does not preside over it.

options.text: The Vice-President of India
options.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha but does not preside over joint sessions.

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sessions of Parliament.

options.text: The Prime Minister of India
options.explanation: The Prime Minister does not preside over joint sessions of Parliament.

questions.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament, while the President summons such a joint sitting.
questions.hint: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is responsible for joint sessions.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: 18 years
options.explanation: 18 is the minimum voting age in India, not the age for Rajya Sabha membership.

options.text: 21 years
options.explanation: 21 is the minimum age for certain local body elections, not for Rajya Sabha membership.

options.text: 25 years
options.explanation: 25 is the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership, not Rajya Sabha.

options.text: 30 years
options.explanation: 30 is the minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.explanation: To be eligible for membership of the Rajya Sabha, a person must be at least 30 years old. For the Lok Sabha, the minimum age is 25 years.
questions.hint: The minimum age for Rajya Sabha members is higher than that for Lok Sabha members.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is considered the 'Upper House' of the Indian Parliament?

options.text: Rajya Sabha
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of the Indian Parliament.

options.text: Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Lok Sabha is the Lower House of the Indian Parliament.

options.text: Vidhan Sabha
options.explanation: The Vidhan Sabha is a state legislative assembly, not part of the Parliament.

options.text: Gram Sabha
options.explanation: The Gram Sabha is a local governance body in rural areas, not part of the Parliament.

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is known as the Upper House or Council of States, while the Lok Sabha is known as the Lower House or House of the People.
questions.hint: The 'Upper House' refers to the Rajya Sabha in the Indian Parliament.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: In a parliamentary form of government, the executive is primarily responsible to which of the following?

options.text: The Judiciary
options.explanation: The judiciary is independent and does not hold the executive accountable in a parliamentary system.

options.text: The President
options.explanation: The President is a constitutional head and does not hold the executive accountable.

options.text: The Legislature
options.explanation: The executive is responsible to the legislature in a parliamentary system.

options.text: The Electorate directly
options.explanation: The electorate holds the legislature accountable, not the executive directly.

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive (Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister) is accountable and responsible to the legislature (Parliament, specifically the Lok Sabha).
questions.hint: The executive's accountability in a parliamentary system is to the legislature.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: During which hour in the Parliament can members raise questions about various administrative activities of the government?

options.text: Question Hour
options.explanation: The Question Hour is the time when members can ask questions to ministers.

options.text: Zero Hour
options.explanation: The Zero Hour is a time after Question Hour when members can raise matters of urgent public importance.

options.text: Budget Session
options.explanation: The Budget Session is a specific session for discussing the budget, not for general questioning.

options.text: Adjournment Motion
options.explanation: An Adjournment Motion is a procedure to discuss a matter of urgent public importance, not a specific hour.

questions.explanation: The Question Hour is the first hour of a sitting in both houses of Parliament, dedicated to asking and answering questions to various ministers regarding government policies and administration.
questions.hint: This is a specific hour dedicated to questioning the government in Parliament.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding a Money Bill in the Indian Parliament?

options.text: It can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
options.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
options.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

options.text: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in passing a Money Bill.
options.explanation: The Rajya Sabha has limited powers and cannot pass a Money Bill independently.

options.text: The President's recommendation is not required for its introduction.
options.explanation: The President's recommendation is mandatory for the introduction of a Money Bill.

questions.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and that too, only on the recommendation of the President. The Rajya Sabha has limited powers regarding a Money Bill; it can only recommend changes, but the Lok Sabha is not bound by these recommendations.
questions.hint: A Money Bill can only be introduced in one House of Parliament.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: A bill passed by both Houses of Parliament cannot become a law until it receives the assent of which authority?

options.text: The Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The Chief Justice of India does not have the power to give assent to bills.

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the House but does not give assent to bills.

options.text: The Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Prime Minister is part of the executive but does not give assent to bills.

options.text: The President of India
options.explanation: The President of India must give assent to a bill passed by Parliament for it to become a law.

questions.explanation: For any bill to become an Act (law), it must be passed by both Houses of Parliament and then receive the assent of the President of India.
questions.hint: The final authority to approve a bill passed by Parliament is the President.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha is known as a permanent house and cannot be dissolved. Reason (R): One-third of its members retire every two years, and new members are elected to replace them.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The Reason is the correct explanation for the Assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is indeed a permanent body, unlike the Lok Sabha, and cannot be dissolved. This permanence is maintained because one-third of its members retire every two years, and elections are held to fill those vacant seats, ensuring continuity without complete dissolution.
questions.hint: The Reason correctly explains why the Assertion is true.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Imagine a situation where the ruling coalition in the Lok Sabha loses the support of the majority of its members, indicated by the passing of a No-Confidence Motion. What would be the most likely immediate consequence for the Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister?

options.text: The President would immediately dissolve the Rajya Sabha.
options.explanation: The President does not dissolve the Rajya Sabha; it is a permanent body.

options.text: The Prime Minister would continue in power until the next general elections.
options.explanation: The Prime Minister must resign if a No-Confidence Motion is passed.

options.text: The Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers would have to resign.
options.explanation: The Council of Ministers must resign if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

options.text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha would take over as the acting Prime Minister.
options.explanation: The Speaker does not take over as Prime Minister; the Council of Ministers resigns.

questions.explanation: In a parliamentary democracy, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a No-Confidence Motion is passed, it signifies that the government has lost the confidence of the majority of the House. Consequently, the Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers must resign.
questions.hint: The passing of a No-Confidence Motion leads to the resignation of the Council of Ministers.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: What is the collective name for the two houses of the Indian Parliament?

options.text: Legislative Assembly
options.explanation: Legislative Assembly is a term used for the lower house of state legislatures, not the Parliament.

options.text: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
options.explanation: Correct. These are the two houses of the Indian Parliament.

options.text: State Legislature
options.explanation: State Legislature refers to the law-making body at the state level, not the Parliament.

options.text: Supreme Court
options.explanation: Supreme Court is the highest judicial body, not a legislative house.

questions.explanation: The Indian Parliament is bicameral, consisting of two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
questions.hint: The Parliament of India has two distinct houses.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Which body is primarily responsible for making laws for the entire country in India?

options.text: The Judiciary
options.explanation: The Judiciary interprets laws but does not make them.

options.text: The Executive
options.explanation: The Executive implements laws but does not primarily make them.

options.text: The Parliament
options.explanation: Correct. The Parliament is responsible for making laws for the country.

options.text: The State Governments
options.explanation: State Governments make laws for their respective states, not the entire country.

questions.explanation: The Parliament of India is the supreme legislative body, meaning its main function is to make laws for the Union of India.
questions.hint: The body that creates laws for the entire nation is the highest legislative authority.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: A bill, after being passed by both Houses of Parliament, becomes a law only after receiving the assent of which authority?

options.text: The Prime Minister
options.explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of government but does not give assent to bills.

options.text: The Chief Justice of India
options.explanation: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary and does not approve bills.

options.text: The President
options.explanation: Correct. The President's assent is required for a bill to become a law.

options.text: The Speaker of Lok Sabha
options.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over the Lok Sabha but does not give assent to bills.

questions.explanation: For a bill to become an Act (law), it must be passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, and then receive the final approval and signature (assent) of the President of India.
questions.hint: The final authority to approve a bill into law is the constitutional head of the country.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Lok Sabha is considered more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in financial matters. Reason (R): Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and cannot be rejected by the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true as the Lok Sabha holds greater power over financial legislation. Reason (R) is also true and directly explains why Lok Sabha is more powerful in financial matters, as Money Bills can only originate in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha has limited powers regarding them (it can only suggest changes but cannot reject a Money Bill).
questions.hint: Consider the powers of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in financial matters.
questions.subject: icse8-sst

questions.question: During a parliamentary session, if the ruling government fails to pass a 'No-Confidence Motion' moved by the opposition, what is the most likely immediate outcome?

options.text: The President dissolves the Rajya Sabha.
options.explanation: The President does not have the power to dissolve the Rajya Sabha.

options.text: The Prime Minister has to resign along with the Council of Ministers.
options.explanation: Correct. The government must resign if it loses a No-Confidence Motion.

options.text: A new Speaker is elected for the Lok Sabha.
options.explanation: The Speaker is elected at the beginning of a new Lok Sabha session, not due to a No-Confidence Motion.

options.text: The opposition leader automatically becomes the new Prime Minister.
options.explanation: The opposition leader does not automatically become Prime Minister; a new government must be formed with majority support.

questions.explanation: A No-Confidence Motion signifies that the Lok Sabha no longer has confidence in the Council of Ministers. If this motion passes (meaning the government fails to secure a majority), the Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers must resign, as the government has lost the confidence of the house.
questions.hint: A No-Confidence Motion challenges the government's majority in the Lok Sabha.
